title: Fluency: when the variance is estimated

families.skill: a t statistic for a mean
families.prompt: A {who}'s {n} {units} average $\bar x = {xb}\%$, with sample sd $s = {s}\%$. What is $t$ for $H_0: \mu = 0$, to 3 decimal places?

wrong.line: You divided by $s$, the sd of one period. Divide by $s/\sqrt n$, with $n = {n}$.
You divided $s$ by $\sqrt{{{df}}}$. The degrees of freedom are $n - 1$, but the standard error uses $\sqrt n = \sqrt{{{n}}}$.

families.skill: a t statistic from a Sharpe ratio
families.prompt: A fund reports {kind} Sharpe ratio of {sr} over {y} {units}. What is its $t$ statistic for a mean of 0, to 3 decimal places?

wrong.line: You multiplied by {y}. The $t$ statistic is the Sharpe ratio times $\sqrt T$, with $T = {y}$.
You divided by $\sqrt T$. The standard error divides $s$ by $\sqrt T$, so $t$ multiplies the Sharpe ratio by it.

solution: $t = \dfrac{{\bar x}}{{s/\sqrt T}}$ is the Sharpe ratio times $\sqrt T$, with $T = {y}$ {units}.
